h1: The 6 Best Under-Desk Printer Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six under-desk printer stands and file cabinets from under $25 to $100, compared on height, storage, casters and ventilation.
summary: The HUANUO stand with a drawer and cable channel is our top pick for most desks. The HOOBRO has the lowest profile, the VASAGLE doubles as a two-drawer file cabinet, and the Letaya adds a lock. The Hovadova ventilated frame is the cheap pick for laser printers.
intro: Under-desk printer stands fail on one measurement most buyers never take: the gap between the floor and the underside of the desk, with the printer's lid fully open. A stand that fits the printer but not the open lid means you drag it out every time you print.

We reviewed six options that can hold a printer under a desk, from open shelves to file cabinets with a top platform. Ranking is based on the spec sheet: stand height, storage, casters, ventilation and price tier. We dropped a monitor riser that was designed for desktops, not floor use.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: The most complete small stand, with drawer, cable channel and locking wheels.
products.description:
The HUANUO stands up to 14.1 inches high and has a rear cable channel, locking caster wheels and a drawer beneath the top shelf. It suits compact and mid-size printers.

It beats the HOOBRO because of the drawer and lockable wheels, though the HOOBRO sits lower. It costs the same $25-50.

Buy it for a standard-height desk. The caveat is the 14.1 inch height, so measure clearance first.
products.idealFor: Standard desks with room for a mid-size printer.
products.skipIf: Your desk clearance is very low.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS 2-Drawer File Cabinet Printer Stand
products.verdict: A real file cabinet sold as a printer stand.
products.description:
The VASAGLE CUSTOS measures 15.7 inches wide, 16.5 deep and 27.6 tall, with two drawers for A4 or letter documents, a matte black finish and a rolling base.

It ranks under the HUANUO because the 27.6 inch height only suits taller desks, but it replaces a separate file cabinet.

Choose it if paperwork lives next to the printer. The caveat is that the drawers are unlocked in the listing.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Three lockable drawers that roll under a desk.
products.description:
The Letaya has three lockable metal drawers, arrives fully assembled and takes letter, legal and A4 documents on a mobile base.

It ranks below the VASAGLE because it is not marketed as a printer stand, though the flat top works. It adds a lock the VASAGLE lacks.

Ideal if you want private documents and a printer in one unit. The caveat is the $50-100 price and the height of three drawers.
products.skipIf: You only need a printer platform.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A slim locking cabinet that fits narrow gaps.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow vertical cabinet with two lockable drawers in black metal, listed for easy assembly and for letter, A4 and legal files.

It ranks under the Letaya because it has fewer drawers and no wheels in the listing, but it is cheaper in the $25-50 bucket and slimmer.

Good for a narrow gap beside the legs. The caveat is that a narrow top limits printer size.

products.name: HOOBRO 2-Tier Printer Stand with Charging Station
products.verdict: A low open two-tier shelf with a charging shelf.
products.description:
The HOOBRO is a 2-tier open shelf with a built-in charging station shelf and a low, compact profile in a rustic brown and black finish. It suits compact printers.

It ranks below the HUANUO because it has no drawer or casters listed, yet it fits tighter clearance.

Buy it for a low desk. The caveat is that open shelves collect dust.

products.name: Hovadova Adjustable Mobile CPU Stand, Ventilated Computer Tower Stand
products.verdict: A cheap rolling frame that lets air through.
products.description:
This was designed as a tower stand, with a ventilated frame, four caster wheels and adjustable width. It costs under $25.

It ranks last because it is not meant for printers and offers no storage, but the open frame helps heat escape from a laser printer.

Buy it as a cheap platform. The caveat is that you must check the printer's footprint against the adjustable range.

whatMatters.detail: Measure from floor to the desk underside, then subtract stand height and the printer's open-lid height. Most failures happen on the lid. Check listed height in the specs.
The top platform must fit the printer's feet. A narrow top can hang the printer over the edge. Compare printer width and depth to the listing.
Laser printers run hot and need airflow. A solid enclosed cabinet traps heat. Prefer an open frame or leave the rear clear.
Wheels make loading paper easier. Locking wheels stop the stand rolling when you pull a drawer. Look for locking in the listing.
A printer needs power and data cables. A rear channel keeps them tidy. Check the listing for cable management.

faq.q: How do I measure for a stand?
faq.a: Measure floor to desk underside, then subtract stand height and the printer height with the lid open.
Ignoring the open lid or paper tray. The printer fits but cannot be used without sliding it out.

faq.q: Is a file cabinet stand worth it?
faq.a: If you keep papers near the printer, yes. If not, a simple stand is cheaper.

faq.q: Can a laser printer sit in a cabinet?
faq.a: Leave the rear clear and avoid fully enclosing it, since heat builds up.

faq.q: How do I stop the stand rolling?
faq.a: Use locking casters, as on the HUANUO.

faq.q: Can I use a CPU stand for a printer?
faq.a: Yes if the printer fits the platform width. Check the weight too.

finalTake: The HUANUO is the best under-desk printer stand for most desks thanks to its drawer, cable channel and locking wheels. The VASAGLE and Letaya suit those who want a file cabinet, the HOOBRO suits tight clearance, and the Hovadova suits hot laser printers. Measure your clearance first.
